records.title: Concrete Clight execution reaches exit/return with the outcome (existential witness, Jsub-free)
records.summary: Terminate.v constructs, for every valid initial world w0, an EXPLICIT finite Clight-core execution of relay_exit.prog reaching the exit(status) call in world final with outcome w0 status final pending, with no Jsub premise and no VST safety axiom -- a direct construction on the AST. TerminateMain.v repeats this for the ORIGINAL relay_main.prog, which halts at Returnstate(Vint status) Kstop with outcome (the 'original main halt' result). ShellExit.v connects the concrete status to the shell layer (relay_exit_shell_witness).
records.proof_statement: relay_exit_termination : forall w0, valid_world w0 -> exists q0, initial_core ... /\ exists k q m final status pending, ok_steps w0 k (q0,init_mem,w0) (q,m,final) /\ at_external ... = Some(exit_ef,[Vint(Int.repr status)]) /\ outcome w0 status final pending.  relay_main_termination: analogous, ending at Returnstate with q=CRet(Vint status) Kstop and halted.
records.assumptions: valid_world w0 only, plus the same standard classical set; explicitly NOT present: Jsub, inline_external_call_mem_events, ef_deterministic_fun, proof_irr, eq_rect_eq, Extensionality_Ensembles.
records.distinctions: WITNESS (existential: one execution per initial world), not universal over all executions -- that is PH5-RELAY-008. Does not use relay_dry_safety (PH5-RELAY-005) at all, so it is Jsub-free even though the safety-side theorems still carry Jsub.

records.title: Universal (all-executions) termination + returned outcome, Jsub-free
records.summary: UniversalMain.relay_main_universal and UniversalExit.relay_exit_universal: for every valid initial world w0 there exist q0, a bound N and the outcome (status,final,pending) such that EVERY Trace.dry_steps execution of any length k from the initial state satisfies k<=N, is never stuck below N, and at k=N has returned/exited with exactly that status -- i.e. every maximal execution in the specified scheduled environment terminates after exactly N steps with the outcome, not just an existential witness. Proved via a generic mem_equiv transfer argument (MemEquivStep.v) plus a canonical-trajectory induction. UniversalShell.v extends this to the shell-level 'relay && mark' query.
records.proof_statement: relay_main_universal / relay_exit_universal: forall w0, valid_world w0 -> exists q0 N status final pending, outcome w0 status final pending /\ (forall k q m z, dry_steps k (q0,init_mem,w0) (q,m,z) -> k<=N /\ ext_ok(q,m,z) /\ (k<N -> exists s', dry_step (q,m,z) s') /\ (k=N -> q=Returnstate(Vint status) Kstop /\ z=final)).
records.assumptions: valid_world w0 only; NO Jsub; NO ef_deterministic_fun (a bespoke builtin-free determinism lemma step_fun_nb was proved instead); standard classical set + CompCert Events parameters. MemEquivAssign.v (needed only for utilities with pointer stores, e.g. future case studies) additionally uses CompCert's lib.Axioms.proof_irr -- explicitly noted as not used by the relay theorems themselves.
records.distinctions: This is the strongest termination result in the project: UNIVERSAL over all executions (not one witness) and Jsub-free (stronger than PH5-RELAY-005's safety theorem, which still needs Jsub). It is still bounded to the STATED scheduled-environment model (every read/write returns with the specified storebytes/loadbytes effect; nothing about host-OS/kernel/signal behaviour; C→Clight translation trusted by hash identity). Read literally: 'universal' = universal over executions consistent with the dry_step environment model, not universal over arbitrary hardware/OS behaviour.

records.title: Shell layer over the relay contract: composition, lexer/parser soundness, differential tests
records.summary: Shell.v ports phase3 ShellObservation.Command/Exec as a generic command/exec relation with command_refines/query_transfer; the relay primitive is exactly the relay_spec POST predicate. Parse.v/Lex.v: parse_program_sound (parser not trusted) and a separately proved lexer soundness (Lex.v). Bridge.v: literal text "relay && mark" parses (vm_compute) to relay_then_mark and transfers the status-sensitive query. Differential tests: 29/29 directed accepted texts agree with real bash 5.2.21; 200/200 randomized fragment texts agree (RandomFixtures.v). ShellAudit.v: 44/44 theorems closed, zero axioms.
records.distinctions: Fragment excludes newline, |, &, redirections, quotes, $, #, !, braces, non-ASCII, digit-first names, assignments -- rejected explicitly, nothing silently erased. A real bug was found and fixed during differential testing: '((t))' was wrongly accepted as grouping (bash runs it as arithmetic, status 1); lexer now rejects adjacent '(('. Completeness/uniqueness of the grammar is not proved; identification of the fragment's lexer/parser relations with real Bash's own grammar remains a stated, inspected-not-proved trust boundary.

records.title: Pipe (|) semantics with backpressure and modelled SIGPIPE
records.summary: Pipeline.v: a new two-sided scheduler (pworld/pstep_fn/prun) over the unchanged Protocol.v primitives, finite capped buffer (PIPE_CAP=4), proved capacity invariant (pstep_fn_capacity/prun_capacity), concrete backpressure/partial-push and SIGPIPE-modelled demos, byte-conservation across both loss ledgers. Bridge2.v: PipeRR is one more atom of Shell.v's generic command/exec, so command_refines/query_transfer already cover it -- no new composition rule invented.
records.distinctions: SIGPIPE and the pipe capacity are NAMED, STATED models (pstep_fn is one fixed deterministic scheduling priority, not a nondeterministic 'any legal interleaving' relation), not claims about the real kernel. No real fds/dup2/process model.

records.title: Bounded text frontend for pipe/redirect (parser only, no soundness proof)
records.summary: ParseExpansion.v: a NEW lexer/parser (not a change to frozen Parse.v/Lex.v) for 'relay'/'mark', 'relay | relay', optional trailing '> IDENT'/'>> IDENT'. 4 vm_compute-checked accept cases, 4 reject cases; bash -n independently confirms the 4 rejections are this fragment's own scope limit, not something real Bash itself rejects.
